newsitem.title: SPAIN: BCH to focus on lower costs and greater efficiency.
newsitem.headline: BCH to focus on lower costs and greater efficiency.

text.p: Banco Central Hispanoamericano (BCH) chairman Jose Maria Amusategui said on Saturday the bank would focus on reducing costs and promoting greater efficiency in its operations to secure higher profits.
"A reduction in costs and increases in productivity are the cornerstones of our strategy," he told a shareholders meeting.

Managing Director Angel Corcostegui said more streamlined costs, together with a greater availability of resources due to a reduction in debts, would boost profits by an estimated 25 percent this year.
"In the current and coming financial years, we will progressively consolidate the recovery initiated in 1996, with firm and gradual increases in profits and dividends," he said.
Corcostegui said the parent company would save some 10 billion pesetas in 1997.
In addition, BCH has reduced its workforce by some 10,000 since 1991 and has shut 1,000 offices. In 1996, operating costs represented 2.37 percent of total assets compared with 2.44 percent in 1995.
"We are capable of generating growing profits through the development of our core banking activities, based on a healthy balance," the chairman said.
Amasutegui underlined the bank's "industrial vocation", with stakes in groups such as Endesa and Cepsa, and said it would remain committed to an international strategy.
"We will consolidate our important presence in Latin America," he said, announcing that the bank's "next operation would be in Colombia". He gave no further details.
Last October, BCH said it had reached an agreement in principle with Banco de Colombia to buy a "significant" stake in the Colombian bank. A final agreement has not yet been announced.
BCH reported a 169 percent increase in net attributable profit to 33.5 billion pesetas in 1996.
